decision.question: Why did the start sound play on the phone's insecure http page with no error shown?
options: trace the whole state machine headless
decision.chose: trace the whole state machine headless
decision.why: proved with Playwright: over http on the LAN IP, isSecureContext=false and navigator.mediaDevices=undefined, but window.webkitSpeechRecognition still exists (a constructor, not gated by secure context) — so Dictate.detect_engine() still picks "browser". Dictate.start() set state to "listening" BEFORE the engine actually connected, so ComposerMic's old beep check ("if state===listening, beep") fired the instant start() returned, not once the mic was real. In this exact simulated case the state then sat at "listening" for 1.5s+ with no error ever arriving.
decision.rule: code#7 (failures that never throw) — a state flag set on intent, not on the real event, is exactly this family of bug

log.msg: Fixed in Dictate.js: start() now sets "connecting" (new state) and only calls set_state("listening") once the mic is REALLY on — after whisper's capture.start() resolves, or from the browser engine's own rec.onstart. ext/Chat/Mic.js's start beep moved to a new on_listening() hook Dictate calls exactly on that real transition (never re-fires on Chrome's own silent mid-session restarts). Added an instant insecure_context_message() check at the top of start() so the LAN-http case now errors immediately with a one-line fix instead of hanging silent.

Added: device-busy (NotReadableError/TrackStartError) and SecurityError to explain(); "Whisper stopped answering" is now a visible set_error() (was only console.error) when close_segment()'s transcribe fails mid-session — the exact "Whisper server unreachable" case from the brief. name_engine() now says "Whisper on the PC" / "the browser's recognizer" per servex-mastermind's addition.

decision.rule: servex-mastermind message on this task's board

decision.question: Reserve the mobile rail's height: a plain flex child of .app, position:fixed + a manual padding reservation (mirroring the side drawer's --rail-push), or rebuild pages as full-height independently-scrolling sections?
options: plain non-fixed flex child of .app (last row in its height:100% flex column)
position:fixed + a new padding-block-end token on .pages, mirroring --rail-push
full-height sections with independent scrolling, site-wide
decision.why: .app is already height:100%; display:flex; flex-direction:column with .pages as its one growing row (framework.css) — a normal last child with flex:0 0 auto already reserves its own space for free, nothing to keep in sync. The fixed+token route re-derives the exact bookkeeping the flex-child route skips, and is only worth it for a bar that must float OVER content (the side drawer does; this one does not). Full-height sections would mean rebuilding how every page scrolls for a bar that only needed its own height reserved — rejected as far more invasive for no extra benefit.
decision.rule: css#4 (constrain the container), code#3 (parts as classes)

decision.question: Why did the new insecure-context error show NOTHING at first, even though the check itself fired?
options: assume the message text was wrong
decision.why: a page-error appeared: "this.capture?.stop is not a function". core/View/View.js sets View.prototype.capture = true (an unrelated auto-append-to-captor flag), and Dictate.start_whisper() already reused the SAME name for its own audio-capture object (this.capture = new Capture(...)) — a pre-existing collision from the "names that collide with core" family. Calling set_error() before start_whisper() has ever run (my new up-front secure-context check does exactly this) hit this.capture as the boolean `true` inherited from View, and `true.stop()` threw BEFORE the status text line ever ran — so the whole error message was silently lost, every time, for any error that can fire before the mic object exists.
decision.rule: code#7, "names that collide with core" — grepped core/View/View.js and found `View.prototype.capture = true` confirming it

log.msg: Fixed: renamed the audio-capture instance field from this.capture to this.mic across Dictate.js (17 sites) and ext/Chat/Mic.js (3 sites) — grepped both files first for stray `capture:` object-literal keys and any `prototype.capture`/`prototype.mic` default, found none. node --check both files after. This was a real, previously-silent bug in shipped code, not something introduced by this task; worth a proactive audit of `View.prototype` field names (capture, and whatever else is on it) against every subclass's own instance fields site-wide, flagged for the auditor/skill-improvement rather than done here (out of this fence).

findings.text: The variant pages don't show what makes each variant different until someone talks into a real mic. `ux/Dictate/variants/cards/page.js:20` draws an empty widget, and in `…-variants-cards/sheet.png` it looks exactly like v1: one 🎤 and "Whisper on the PC". All eight review screenshots are at 1280/1920/3440 px. None is at 400 px, which is the width this task is about. The only mobile proof is the task's own `ext/drawer/rail/shots/*.png`. A 400 px review shot of `/` and `/framework/` with the rail and the sidebar ☰ would settle deliverables 1 and 2 directly.

There's a simpler option: `ext/drawer/rail.js:140-152` (the `DrawerRailSheet` `listen()` and `card()`) redraws by hand the same card list that `CardsDictate` already provides. `Cards.js` even says the sheet "could be built from" it. Building the sheet from `new CardsDictate({})` would remove the duplicate code and the second card style, and it would put the variant to real use.

The sheet builds a plain `Dictate` in `mode: "open"` (`rail.js:141`), and that widget draws its own caption line too. Every finished sentence may therefore appear twice: once in the caption and once as a card. Check the open sheet with real speech, or use `CardsDictate` (see finding 4).

"v1 — today's box" (`variants/v1/page.js:18`) is the live base `Dictate`, not a frozen copy. It already shows this task's changes (the new engine label "Whisper on the PC" and the "connecting" state). Any later change to `Dictate.js` will change "v1" as well, so it doesn't fully meet the "keep version 1" rule.

If the phone rotates or the window is widened past 52em while the sheet is open, `rail.css:59` hides the sheet but the mic keeps listening, and there is no visible way to stop it. Stopping the dictation when the media query stops matching would close that gap.

The sheet's slide-up transition never plays (`rail.css:57-59`). The sheet switches from `display: none` straight to `transform: none`, so it pops in. This is harmless, but the transition can be deleted or made to work.

The `/whisper/inference` proxy (`Server/plugins/Whisper.js:28`) is intentionally reachable from the LAN without any guard. That fits a dev-only server, but anyone on the Wi-Fi can use the GPU through it. One line in `doc/https-lan.md` saying so would be enough.
The header comment in `variants/compact/page.js:4` says Compact "overrides ONE method". The class overrides two, and the page text itself says two.

Space: the Variants wall and each variant page are 76–86% empty at 1920 and 3440 (`…-variants/sheet.png`, `…-variants-cards/sheet.png`). Larger preview cards with seeded content (finding 1) would fill the space and show the difference between variants at a glance. Navigation is clear: Variants is its own tab and has a sidebar entry, and the playground links to it (`…-playground/sheet.png`).
